chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from a man who named him, from Al-Husayn al-Jammal, who said:

I witnessed Is'hāq ibn 'Ammār one day, and he had packed his bag and was intending to depart, when a man came to him seeking dirhams for a dinar. So he opened the bag and gave him dirhams for a dinar. He said, so I said to him, 'Glory be to Allah, what was the advantage of this dinar?' So Is'hāq said, 'I did not do this out of desire for the advantage of the dinar, but I heard Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: He who considers little sustenance insignificant will be deprived of much.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of not belittling small sustenance in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: This narrative from al-Kāfī highlights the spiritual discipline of contentment (riḍā) through the example of Isḥāq ibn ‘Ammār, who prioritized the Imam’s teaching over market logic by accepting a loss in exchange for spiritual gain. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on how one’s perception of sustenance directly influences its abundance, linking material transactions to metaphysical realities.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abdu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from a man who heard it from Al Husayn Al Jammal who said,

‘I Witnessed Is’haq Bin Ammar one day and he had packed his bag and he wanted to move, when a person came asking to exchange Dirhams with Dinars. So he opened his bag and gave him Dirhams for Dinars. So I said to him, ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! How Dinars can be better?’ So Is’haq said, ‘I did not do this (exchange) in my craving regarding the preference of the Dinar, but I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who belittles the little sustenance, would deprived of a lot’.
en.sarwar: 30. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from a man whom has named from al-Husayn al-Jammal who has said the following:

“One day I saw Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar pack his bag, ready to move, when a man came asking to exchange dirham with dinar. He opened his bag, gave him dirham and took the dinar. I then said, ‘Allah is free of all defects, how dinar can be better?’ Ishaq said, ‘I did not do it because of my interest in dinar, but I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, “One who considers a small amount of sustenance little becomes deprived of a great deal of sustenance.’””
